1) Sandbox org provisioned + seed accounts (Sean) — target: 2026-05-06
2) Initial API key pair issued (long-lived test + ephemeral demo key) (Aditya) — target: 2026-05-07
3) IP allowlist entry + smoke tests from CardioTech staging CIDR (CardioTech IT) — target: 2026-05-08
4) VPC peering dry-run (Redwood infra + CardioTech network) (Marissa) — target: 2026-05-12
5) Final acceptance run + metrics review (joint) — target: 2026-05-14

Notes/asks:
- Please confirm which CIDRs we should allow for staging and production egress. We typically ask for a /24 for staging and a separate /24 for prod.
- For the long-lived test key we'll set a 30-day TTL and label it "cardiotech-test-1"; for demonstrations we'll provide a pre-warm ephemeral key with a 1-hour TTL.
- Marissa will coordinate the peering calendar; Aditya will post the peering templates.

I've attached the MAP workbook and added short owner notes. If any of these dates conflict with your internal calendar, suggest swaps and we’ll adapt.

Thanks — we’ll treat SOC2 as part of the procurement pack; Marissa can share our security packet.

Best,

Hi Lisa — looping in operational details from our side. Quick operational checklist for the VPC peering and credentialing sprint: 

Operational checklist (Marissa):
- Pre-peering: exchange account IDs, preferred VPC CIDRs, and allowed routes (please send to it@cardiotech.com).
- Peering options: (a) Shared-route peering (fast, lower overhead) or (b) Private-transit via transit gateway (more setup, better isolation). Recommend shared-route for evaluation.
- Required artifacts from CardioTech: Owner contact, nat routing table, and security group baseline.
- Our timeline: 3 business days to provision peering on staging, 5 business days for private-transit option.

Credentialing notes:
- We will create a sandbox org and seed two admin accounts. Aditya will create the first test API key and mark it as "cardiotech-test-1".
- For the ephemeral flow we recommend using our token-exchange endpoint; docs link in Drive.

Security packet: I’ll attach our SOC2 summary and a link to the full packet. Also nudging procurement — there’s a DocuSign for the MSA and an initial quote in HubSpot (deal RDW-23184).

Marissa Cole

Thanks — some tech specifics from our engineering playbook to make the handover smooth.

Org & API key seeding:
- We will provision a sandbox org under your account with two seeded users: cardiotech_admin and cardiotech_ops. Please confirm the preferred admin email addresses.
- API key plan: create one labeled cardiotech-test-1 (expires 2026-05-30) and one ephemeral pattern via token exchange (TTL 1 hour). Example curl to validate token:

  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <CARDIOTECH_TEST_KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health

IP allowlist guidance:
- Please provide egress CIDRs for your staging and prod runners. Recommended: staging 198.51.100.0/24, prod 198.51.101.0/24 (placeholder — replace with your ranges).
- For initial smoke tests open ports 443 (HTTPS) and 22 is not required unless you request bastion access.

VPC peering specifics:
- Suggested peering CIDR: your VPC (10.20.0.0/16) <-> Redwood staging VPC (10.40.0.0/16). Avoid overlapping with your on-prem ranges.
- Route table changes: Add a 10.40.0.0/16 route in your staging RT to the peering connection.
- Time estimate: we can complete peering config and validate BGP-less routing within 48-72 hours for the shared-route option.

Test endpoint and metrics:
- We will provide a pre-warmed endpoint for throughput testing: https://staging-api.redwood.ai/cardiotech/test
- Please run the sample prompt set in the Drive folder — that will generate the latencies we’ll review on 2026-05-14.

Ping me the admin emails and the actual CIDRs and I’ll create the keys and post back the key ID and fingerprint.

— Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
